departments.title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
departments.summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.

departments.title: DESIGNCRAFT — game-design intelligence
departments.summary: levels, missions, story, progression and experience, from the game's own data

findings.title: 2 missions share the same structure: mount → travel → scan → travel
findings.evidence: Eyes on Kessel Bowl and Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded have an identical sequence of objective types. 6 of 10 missions repeat a structure another mission already uses. (facts verified in source: 2)
findings.recommendation: Give each of Eyes on Kessel Bowl and Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded one objective the others do not have.

findings.title: 37 of 58 named places are never a mission destination
findings.evidence: No mission objective targets lodge-dusk, lodge-night, Tannberg Headwall, West Face, Lift Line Gully and 32 more. They exist in the world data but the mission structure never asks the player to go there. (facts verified in source: 6)
findings.recommendation: Route existing missions through the unused places.

findings.title: One story path: no endings, choices or branches in the data
findings.evidence: No ending definitions and no scripted choices were found, although the docs talk about choice or consequence 3 times. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add one decision with two outcomes at the story's midpoint.

findings.title: Only 0 of 46 objectives offer more than one way to complete them
findings.evidence: Almost every objective has exactly one target and one method in its definition. (facts verified in source: 5)
findings.recommendation: Give key objectives a second valid target or method.

findings.title: The player decides how fast, never what or how
findings.evidence: No objective offers alternatives, none is optional, and the story has no endings or choices in the data; free play exists (20 references) but is separate from the missions. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add alternatives and optional goals to the five most-played missions.

findings.title: 56% of the mapped area holds nothing to find or do
findings.evidence: Dividing the playable extent (1720×1192 units) into a 6×6 grid, 20 cells contain no placed location and no mission target; the emptiest quarter is the south-west (6 of 9 cells empty). (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add landmarks and small finds to the south-west of the map.

findings.title: 7 of 10 missions mention no character
findings.evidence: The briefs, objectives and completion text of Eyes on Kessel Bowl, Controlled Release, Firewood for the Kettle, Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded and 3 more name none of the 7 characters. (facts verified in source: 5)
findings.recommendation: Put a person in Eyes on Kessel Bowl, Controlled Release and Firewood for the Kettle: who asked, who is helped.

findings.title: Buying everything costs 5.6× what the campaign pays
findings.evidence: The non-repeating missions pay 1390 funds in total; the 38 priced unlocks cost 7750. The gap is meant to be filled by 4 repeatable mission(s) (Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded, Bring Down the Bowl, Tree Down on the Pass and Stuck in the Drift). (facts verified in source: 2)
findings.recommendation: Bring prices and income closer: raise campaign rewards or lower top prices.

findings.title: Missions define no way to fail
findings.evidence: No mission definition has a fail condition, time limit or loss state; the source has 21 fail-state references, so failure may live in code outside the mission data. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add a soft fail state to missions with a clock or a threat.

findings.title: No optional or bonus objectives
findings.evidence: None of the 46 objectives is marked optional or bonus. (facts verified in source: 1)
findings.recommendation: Add one optional bonus objective to each mission.

findings.title: PLAYCRAFT measured 5.1 s from load to first input
findings.evidence: In PLAYCRAFT run 20261105001110-pass-06bc6f6e the game took 5.1 s before it accepted play (software renderer; real devices are usually faster).
findings.recommendation: Let the player act during loading.

findings.title: 2 briefings run past 45 words
findings.evidence: Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded and Bring Down the Bowl have long briefs (67, 70 words). (facts verified in source: 2)
